Records.description: Equal-mass 'acnode' (Fig. 3(i)): two-loop four-point diagram, K4-minus-one-edge topology (5 internal propagators, common mass m1), verified 2-loop via L = E - V + 1 = 5 - 4 + 1 = 2. IMPORTANT CAVEAT explicit in the paper: this is presented as a pathological example where the naive top-sector approach BREAKS -- the top-sector solution set becomes positive-dimensional (dim(J_S) != 0), so CountSectorsUnregulated returns 'Indeterminate' rather than a finite master-integral count; the paper states the resulting singularities are nonetheless 'captured with ease' by SOFIA directly. So this family's top-sector Euler characteristic/master-integral count is genuinely ill-defined via the sector-by-sector method described in the main text, not merely un-extracted -- master_integral_count is left null for that reason, not because of missing information. EDGE LIST, VERTEX LABELS AND MASSES WERE SUPPLIED DIRECTLY BY THE USER, NOT EXTRACTED FROM PAPER TEXT: the arXiv LaTeX source shows this diagram only as a PDF figure (figures/diagram_acnode2.pdf) with a descriptive label -- no propagator/graph data appears in the paper's text.
